subject: general
question:
**A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech.**

She said, "I had completed the report."

options.text: She said that she completed the report.
She said that she has completed the report.
She said that she had completed the report.
She said she had been completing the report.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** She said that she had completed the report.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Direct Speech:** "I had completed the report." becomes **Indirect Speech:** "She said that she had completed the report."
 
• **Tense Change:**
 
 
• Past perfect tense ("had completed") remains unchanged in indirect speech because it is already in the correct form.
 
 
 
• **Pronoun Change:**
 
 
• The pronoun "I" in direct speech is changed to "she" in indirect speech to match the subject of the reporting verb "she said."
 
 
 
• **Reporting Verb:**
 
 
• The reporting verb "said" remains as it is in indirect speech.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Quotation marks are removed in indirect speech.
 
• The sentence is introduced with "that" to link the reporting clause and the reported speech.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *She said that she had completed the report.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "She said that she completed the report."
 
 
• Incorrect because the past perfect tense ("had completed") is not maintained, which changes the meaning of the sentence.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "She said that she has completed the report."
 
 
• Incorrect because the present perfect tense ("has completed") is used, which does not align with the past perfect tense of the direct speech.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "She said she had been completing the report."
 
 
• Incorrect because the past perfect continuous tense ("had been completing") changes the meaning of the original sentence, implying an ongoing action rather than a completed action.
 
 
</ul
